title: Setting up a trust business structure
summary: Learn about setting up a trust business structure, including its key features and types.
intro:
A trust is a structure where a trustee (an individual or a company) carries on business for the benefit of other people (the beneficiaries). It's set up through a formal trust deed which outlines how the trust will operate.

There are 2 main types of trusts:

A trust is not a separate legal entity. The trustee is legally responsible for the operation of the trust, and legally liable for the debts of the trust. Commonly however, the trustee is a company (a corporate trustee), which can reduce liability.

A trust can be tax effective due to the flexibility of its asset and income distribution. It can't distribute losses however, only profits.

faqs.a: A trust is a structure where a trustee (an individual or a company) carries on business for the benefit of other people (the beneficiaries). It is set up through a formal trust deed.

faqs.q: Is a trust a separate legal entity?
faqs.a: No, a trust is not a separate legal entity. The trustee is legally responsible for the operation and debts of the trust.

faqs.q: How can a trust reduce liability?
faqs.a: While the trustee is legally responsible, the trustee can commonly be a company (a corporate trustee), which can reduce liability.
